name: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type VI

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type VI

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic erythroid abnormalities including multinuclearity and nuclear bridging in bone marrow erythroblasts
Chronic severe anemia with reticulocytopenia and ineffective erythropoiesis
Identification of pathogenic variants in the SEC23B gene
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and indirect hyperbilirubinemia indicating hemolysis
Bone marrow showing erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoietic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic erythroid abnormalities on bone marrow examination plus severe anemia and confirmation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis due to overlap with other CDA subtypes

pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive morphological feature on bone marrow smear

occasional.notes: Less common than in other CDA types

rare.symptomName: Cardiac complications secondary to chronic anemia

laboratory: Severe anemia with low reticulocyte count
Bone marrow erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoiesis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SEC23B gene confirmed by molecular testing
other: Ineffective erythropoiesis demonstrated by bone marrow biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of binucleated erythroblasts but absence of nuclear bridging
Less severe anemia and different bone marrow morphology
No multinuclear erythroblasts or nuclear bridging

redFlags: Severe transfusion-dependent anemia in infancy or early childhood
Progressive splenomegaly with risk of hypersplenism
Signs of iron overload despite no or minimal transfusions
references: Iolascon A, et al. Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemias: Molecular Insights and Diagnostic Challenges. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2020.
